Hi Clara — thanks for the clear asks and the report. High-level next steps below and two options for you to consider.

Option A (36-month, staged ramp — recommended)
- Year 1: 40% committed capacity with 30% one-time onboarding credit applied to invoices in Q1
- Year 2: 60% commit, price per token steps down 8% from Year 1 list
- Year 3: Full commit; additional 5% loyalty discount if no material usage regressions
- Co-term: we can align your Redwood term with infra BU date; finance requires a single co-term invoice run date.

Option B (24-month, higher upfront commit)
- Year 1: 65% commit, smaller onboarding credit (10%)
- Year 2: Full commit with deeper per-unit price but no loyalty kicker

We will:
- Draft a term sheet and route to Legal for auto-renew opt-out language and co-terming mechanics.
- Confirm invoice cutover date with Accounting (can be Jan 1 if signed by Dec 15).

Would you be available for a 30-min call Thursday to go over trade-offs? If you prefer, we can circulate a redlined term sheet first.

Best,
Hannah

Folks — quick internal note before I send a formal proposal back to Atlas. Highlights from Clara's ask:

- 36mo with staged ramp (40/60/100). They want 30% onboarding credit year1 and co-terming with infra BU so invoices sync Jan 1.
- Legal will insist on an auto-renew opt-out window; procurement will ask for audit logs retention periods (SOC2 + retention clarity).

Questions I have:
1) How much flexibility on upfront credit? Can we do 30% credit year1 if we require a 36-mo commitment and 120% minimum committed token uplift in year 3?
2) Are we comfortable with co-terming mechanics that require us to pro-rate or issue a true-up invoice? What does Accounting need to handle a Jan 1 cutover mid-cycle?
3) Any red flags on the auto-renew wording that would block the discount/credit?

Suggested initial position: 30% onboarding credit tied to an irrevocable 36mo commitment, with a true-up clause at Year 3 and a canary fallback to our Hosted API if Dedicated capacity is constrained.

Marissa/Monica — can you weigh in with the legal/accounting constraints and a recommended concession band? I want to present a clean option to Clara by Monday.

Hannah — good summary. Quick replies to your questions: 

1) Credit band: We can allocate up to 30% one-time onboarding credit in Year 1 if Atlas signs a 36-month agreement with a minimum Year 3 uplift (120% of current paid usage) and an early termination fee that amortizes the credit. That protects us if they under-deploy.

2) Accounting: Co-terming to Jan 1 is OK. We will need a single invoice run and a pro-rated first invoice if the term begins mid-quarter. If they sign after Dec 15 we cannot guarantee Jan 1 cutover; advise Clara to finish sign-off by Dec 15 to meet FY cutover. Also recommend a true-up cadence (annual).

3) Legal: Auto-renew opt-out window = 60 days notice before renewal; legal is comfortable with that as long as we have a defined notice channel. We'll add a fallback clause for capacity: primary Dedicated pool, fallback to Hosted API with defined latency/throughput SLAs.

I'll prepare a revised term sheet that incorporates the amortized early-termination clause and the onboarding credit conditions. Sending draft Monday.

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_draft_v2.pdf

-Marissa

Clara — thanks for the patience. Attached is an updated term sheet that reflects a structured 36-month option we think suits your goals. Summary of the proposal: 

- Term: 36 months; staged commit at 40% Year1 / 60% Year2 / 100% Year3
- Onboarding credit: one-time 30% credit applied in Q1 invoices; credit is amortized and subject to an early termination repayment schedule (see section 6).
- Co-terming: Redwood will align the master contract to your infra BU term (Jan 1 cutover) provided the contract is fully executed by Dec 15, 2027. Otherwise Jan 1 alignment moves to next FY.
- Auto-renew: 60-day notice window to opt out; default auto-renew renews at then-current pricing unless modified by mutual written agreement.
- Fallback: Dedicated capacity guarantee with fallback to Hosted API if capacity shortfall occurs; fallback SLAs and runbook included in Appendix B.

Next steps:
1) If the structure looks good, we can send this to your legal/finance via DocuSign for signature.
2) Accounting will prepare a pro-rated first invoice if the effective date is mid-quarter and will sync the invoice run to Jan 1 if we receive signatures by Dec 15.

I've included the draft term sheet and the Q4 usage file we reviewed. Please let me know any critical must-haves from Legal that would block signature.

Thanks,
Hannah
